# The reciprocal pair stiffness is not globally convex

This is an exact scope check for a proposed funding shortcut. It does not contradict a comparison restricted to three actual stationary sections with one common centroid.

For raw tetrahedral margins (p,q,-1,-1), put s=p+q, v=pq. The negative-pair cap stiffness is

    J(p,q)=2N/[3(s+2v)(1+s+v)^2],
    N=s^2+4sv+6v^2-v-v^3.

It equals H_P[e_3-e_4,e_3-e_4]/(3 f_V(0)). This follows by setting U=1/(1+p), V=1/(1+q) in the actual two-negative-phase derivative formula

    2[(U+V-1)^3+UV(3-2U-2V)]/[3(2-U-V)].

The reciprocal R=1/J need not be convex even along a fixed-sum positive-height segment. Take p=1/10+t and q=1/10-t. At t=0 exact differentiation gives

    R(0)=363/29,      R''(0)=-270000/841<0.

Both heights remain positive for |t|<1/10 and their sum is 1/5<1. Thus positivity and a small positive-pair sum do not supply the desired reciprocal convexity. The actual section at t=0 has centroid (5/11,5/11,1/22,1/22); this does not have the multiple stationary planes needed for the proposed three-row funding comparison. Any useful comparison must retain those joint root equations or additional geometric information.
